e: An edge-optimized API Gateway endpoint routes requests through the CloudFront network's nearest edge location, reducing latency for geographically distributed users. Regional endpoints serve from one Region, and private or interface VPC endpoints are for access inside a VPC.

ACM issues public certificates for CloudFront and renews them automatically when DNS validation is used (the validation record stays in place), which is the most operationally efficient. Email validation needs manual action, and CloudFront security policies and OAC don't create certificates.

DAX is a fully managed, API-compatible in-memory cache for DynamoDB that reduces read latency from milliseconds to microseconds with minimal changes. ElastiCache needs caching logic in the application, and moving to Redshift or RDS doesn't give microsecond reads.

The Instance Scheduler on AWS starts and stops RDS instances on a schedule (weekday business hours), so the company doesn't pay for compute while it's off, with little operational work. Custom Lambda is more effort, and backups or reserved instances don't turn the database off.

A latency-sensitive application using locally attached storage maps to EC2 with an EBS volume (block storage), without changing the architecture, and gp3 is cheaper than gp2 with better baseline performance. FSx file systems change the storage model and cost more.

A minimum capacity of four with two On-Demand instances in each of two AZs means that if one AZ fails, two instances are still running, so the application's requirement of at least two always running is met with high availability and fault tolerance. With a minimum of two split across AZs, one AZ failure leaves only one; Spot Instances can be reclaimed.

Latency-based routing sends each user to the endpoint with the lowest latency, which minimizes load time; the on-premises endpoint can be associated with the us-west-1 Region (nearest) and the AWS site with eu-central-1. Geolocation routes by user location rather than measured latency, and simple or weighted policies don't optimize latency.

5 PB over a 1 Gbps link would take over a year, so use Snowball devices with Tape Gateway to copy the tapes to virtual tapes, ship them to AWS, and lifecycle the tapes to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, the cheapest long-term storage for 10 years of compliance retention.

A spread placement group places each instance on distinct underlying hardware, so groups of nodes don't share the same hardware. Dedicated tenancy isolates your instances from other accounts but not from each other, and separate accounts or shared tenancy don't guarantee separate hardware per node.

An On-Demand Capacity Reservation guarantees EC2 capacity in the failover Region (and Availability Zone), which is what ensures capacity during a disaster. On-Demand without a reservation, Savings Plans, and regional Reserved Instances don't reserve capacity.

An account can belong to only one organization at a time, so the R&D account must first leave the old organization and then be invited to the new organization from the new management account. Being in both, or making the management account a member, isn't possible.

API Gateway provides the integration endpoint with a Lambda authorizer for the authorization step, and Kinesis Data Firehose ingests the unpredictable, spiky activity and delivers it to S3 for analytics, all serverless. Gateway Load Balancers don't do authorization, and Kinesis Data Streams would need consumers.

With an RPO and RTO of 24 hours, copying automated RDS snapshots to another Region every 24 hours is the cheapest DR approach (no running replica), and the database can be restored from the snapshot within the RTO. Cross-Region read replicas or DMS keep a standby running continuously.

ElastiCache for Redis provides durable, highly available session storage with replication and automatic failover, so session state survives web server outages. Memcached has no replication or persistence, Storage Gateway isn't a session store, and RDS is slower and costlier for sessions.

A read replica serves the monthly reporting queries so the primary database's daily workload isn't affected, without resizing for a once-a-month need. Restoring backups to another instance or exporting data to S3 with Athena involves more work or stale data, and resizing costs more permanently.

The AWS Load Balancer Controller provisions an Application Load Balancer from Kubernetes Ingress resources, which routes requests by path or host to the right microservices at lower cost than API Gateway. An NLB works at layer 4 and can't route by path.

S3 stores the images cheaply, CloudFront distributes them globally with low latency, geographic restrictions deny access from specific countries, and signed URLs limit access to paying customers. Public buckets, per-customer IAM users, or regional EC2 fleets are insecure or costly.

Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with multiple nodes per shard provide node-level failover and Availability Zone resilience, so a failure doesn't degrade performance or lose data within the Region. AOF, Auto Scaling, or extra replicas alone don't provide automatic multi-AZ failover.

Hibernation saves the in-memory state to the root EBS volume so a restarted instance resumes with the application already loaded, and Auto Scaling warm pools keep pre-initialized (hibernated) instances ready, reducing launch time. Spot, Capacity Reservations, or just more instances don't shorten application warm-up.

Traffic spikes on random days can't be predicted or scheduled, so dynamic scaling (target tracking on a metric) adds capacity when needed and removes it afterward, which is the most cost-effective way to maintain performance. Manual, predictive, or scheduled scaling depend on patterns or human action.

Aurora Serverless v2 is PostgreSQL-compatible and scales capacity automatically in small increments for unpredictable traffic, so the company pays for what it uses. Self-managed EC2 can't auto scale a database simply, a larger RDS instance is paid for continuously, and Redshift is for analytics.

The latency at the start of each day is Lambda cold starts, so scheduled scaling that raises provisioned concurrency before employees begin keeps execution environments warm. Throttling limits, memory, or a warming alarm don't reliably prevent cold starts.

An S3 File Gateway lets the devices write .csv files to an SMB share that is stored in S3, a Glue crawler creates a table from the S3 data, and Athena runs SQL queries on demand (pay per query), the most cost-effective combination. EMR and Redshift clusters cost more for periodic queries, and FSx File Gateway is for FSx for Windows.

On AWS Outposts the customer is responsible for resilient power and networking to the racks, physical security and access controls in the data center, and providing extra capacity for workloads such as ECS to cover failures and maintenance. AWS manages the Outposts infrastructure, hypervisor, services, availability of the hardware, and its physical maintenance.

A Network Load Balancer operates at layer 4, supports TCP on any port, handles millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency, and can be internet-facing, matching the hardware appliance's performance. ALBs are for HTTP/HTTPS, and CloudFront or API Gateway don't serve arbitrary TCP ports at that scale.
